# API Contracts

<!-- Generated by /ai-context. Manual edits are overwritten on re-run. -->

## AS IS — Current state

### Not applicable in this repository

No HTTP or GraphQL surface exists. `applicationId com.mytracksapp` (`app/build.gradle.kts`)
builds a single-Activity Android app with no server module, no HTTP client dependency (no
Retrofit/OkHttp/Ktor in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`), and no `INTERNET` permission declared
directly in `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (Play Services Maps merges one in transitively,
for map tile rendering only — not app-authored networking). There is no message broker/queue
dependency either (no Kafka/RabbitMQ/Firebase Cloud Messaging client) — the only asynchronous
mechanism is an in-process Android `Service` started via `Intent`
(`app/src/main/java/com/mytracksapp/service/LocationForegroundServiceController.kt`), which is
not a network- or queue-based message format.

### Internal navigation surface (closest analogue)

`ui/navigation/AppNavigation.kt`'s `Routes` object is the closest thing to an API index — in-process Compose Navigation destinations, not a network contract:

| Route | Args | Screen | Entry condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `new_session` | none | `NewSessionScreen` | app start / bottom-bar tab |
| `tracking/{sessionId}` | `sessionId: String` | `TrackingScreen` | after `SessionController.startSession` returns `Started(sessionId)` |
| `history` | none | `HistoryListScreen` | app start (default `startDestination`) / bottom-bar tab |
| `session_detail/{sessionId}` | `sessionId: String` | `SessionDetailScreen` | tapping a session row in `HistoryListScreen` |
| `settings` | none | `SettingsScreen` | drawer menu item |

### Intent contract — `LocationForegroundService`

The service's `onStartCommand` extras (`app/src/main/java/com/mytracksapp/service/LocationForegroundService.kt`) are the nearest thing to a request payload in this codebase:

```kotlin
Intent(appContext, LocationForegroundService::class.java).apply {
    putExtra(LocationForegroundService.EXTRA_SESSION_ID, sessionId)      // String
    putExtra(LocationForegroundService.EXTRA_INTERVAL_SECONDS, interval.seconds) // Int
}
```

- Missing/invalid `sessionId` or an `intervalSeconds` not matching any `SamplingInterval` → the service calls `stopSelf()` and returns `START_NOT_STICKY` without collecting anything.
- Valid extras → `startForeground` is called synchronously first, then `START_STICKY` is returned.
